Property-first planning

What to check before renovating in Carnation

Existing rooms and systems

For a Carnation remodel with direct yard or work-area access, compare the durable entry surface with adjoining finished flooring. Locate cleaning storage, ventilation, and circulation before choosing room finishes in isolation.

Parcel and jurisdiction

Check the Carnation parcel's jurisdiction and mapped flood or other site constraints before an addition or ADU concept is fixed. Existing wastewater and water-service capacity should be part of that feasibility assessment.

Access and staging

For Carnation sites with limited paved staging, identify a loading area that remains usable in wet weather. Keep delivery routes clear of septic features, drainage paths, and retained planting where those are present.

Exterior condition

Review lower wall, porch, and entry details where a Carnation exterior receives splashback or water from surrounding grade. Resolve drainage and substrate deterioration before surface finishes are applied.

Official local resources

Check the requirements for your property.

Start with City of Carnation or King County. Requirements depend on the parcel and scope; confirm the current pathway before relying on a permit assumption.
